artifacts.summary: Research report tracing all six dispatch mutation sites, confirming reusable existing verbs (--flush-seq, --clear-pending, task-lock.sh release, state-write.sh), identifying the pre-image capture gap, the lock session-identity subtlety, and documentation-placement findings for docs/architecture/orchestrate-state-machine.md, context/standards/git-safety.md, and SKILL.md Move 1.

memory_candidates.content: In agent-system/extensions/core, orchestrate-loop-guard-init.sh's --record-pending verb accepts an arbitrary JSON object verbatim (it does not construct the pending_dispatch shape itself) -- widening the pending_dispatch record's fields only ever requires a caller-side change in orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh, never a change to orchestrate-loop-guard-init.sh itself.

In agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh, task-lock.sh acquire/check/heartbeat always use the BARE session_id, but skill_preflight_update's session_id argument (and hence the value written into state.json) is SUFFIXED (${session_id}_${t}) for research/plan phases and bare only for implement. Any recovery/inspection tool that needs to release a lock or match a session recorded in state.json must not assume these two values are interchangeable -- read the lock's own holder session via `task-lock.sh check` instead of deriving it from state.json.

In agent-system/extensions/core, .orchestrator-loop-guard, .lock/, .dispatch/, and .orchestrator-multi-state*.json are all covered by specs/.gitignore's managed runtime-file-patterns.sh block. A recovery/cleanup script touching only these plus specs/state.json and specs/TODO.md never needs to worry about git status leftovers beyond those last two tracked files.
